entries.label: v0.1.12
entries.title: Direct tools, gentler ground and subtitle fixes

sections.heading: Changed
items: Select Hoe, Seeds, Watering Can and Shovel with 1–4, or D-pad Up, Right, Down and Left. The radial tool menu is retired.
Cycle shovel modes with X on keyboard or X / Square on controller. Put tools away with T or B / Circle; B still goes back in menus.
Natural garden rises are capped at 18 cm. Older saved raised patches are softened once; dug-out areas retain their depth.
Thump sets every corner and edge of the selected micro-tile to height zero, with a transition into neighbouring ground.

sections.heading: Fixed
items: Arthur’s speech bubble stays hidden until he speaks, including after entering the garden or returning from the village.
Putting a tool away cancels its current stroke, particles and sound. Ctrl+T still controls the TARDIS.

sections.heading: Website
items: Added this development changelog and linked it from the game page. Future completed changes will receive notes before manual publication.

sections.heading: Added
items: The first hedgehog visit starts a face-on conversation with Arthur.
Arthur alternates his two supplied talking animations while Arthur_Hedgehogs.mp3 plays. A speech bubble displays subtitles generated from the recording.
The camera and controls return when the recording ends. The scene waits for menus, supports pausing, and saves completion so it only plays once per garden.

sections.heading: Added
items: Village mountains, wooded ridges, meadow verges, grass, drifting clouds and mist, using the garden’s landscape assets.
The village and shops share the garden’s clock and weather, including night lighting, rain, wet surfaces, thunder and ambient sound.

sections.heading: Improved
items: Gravel street edges blend into the meadow.
Gold-and-blue spirit cursors replace the red-and-gold colours. Their mesh follows the ground as they move, rotate and resize.
Fixed village cursor visibility and shop selection; the ring frames the selected shop.

sections.heading: Improved
items: Garden-edge textures continue into the surrounding meadow and blend over 1.5 metres, including corners. Changes to edge tiles appear immediately outside the boundary.
Colour, normal detail, roughness, parallax and wetness match at the join.
Thump flattens the whole micro-tile, including its corners and shared edges. The next update changes its target height to zero.

sections.heading: Added
items: The shovel has four animated modes with sound: Dig, Pick, Pour and Thump.
Dig deforms the ground into a sloping, water-filled hollow. Pick makes a small seed hole; Pour restores dirt; Thump levels the ground.
Hold left-click or right trigger to keep using tools while gliding. Each tool uses its supplied sound effects.
Ctrl+T and right-stick click toggle the TARDIS landing and takeoff.

sections.heading: Improved
items: Terrain collision, water depth and grass roots follow edits. Deformation and seed holes survive saving and loading.
Release packaging now exports to a fresh staging file and excludes temporary packs.

entries.label: v0.1.7
entries.title: Garden milestones and a land survey

sections.heading: Added
items: Bottom-left notices report animal visits, residency and recorded birth or death events. Visit and residency dates appear in the Field Guide.
A Land Area category maps all 1,296 micro-tiles, with ground-type counts and percentages.

sections.heading: Changed
items: The TARDIS lands just north of the garden, facing south, without spinning.

sections.heading: Development note
items: Birth and death notifications are event support; automatic breeding and ageing are not implemented.

sections.heading: Added
items: Compasses in the garden and village show the direction you face.
A developer console opens with the backtick key and accepts time and weather commands.
The supplied TARDIS model has materialisation, lighting and landing/takeoff sound effects, with console controls.

sections.heading: Changed
items: New gardens begin without animals inside. A wild hedgehog patrols outside until grass covers at least 1% of the plot.
The hedgehog becomes a resident at 5% grass coverage. The Field Guide records first visit and residency days, saved with the garden.

sections.heading: Added
items: The peacock joins the animal shop, using the supplied model and animated movement.

sections.heading: Changed
items: Garden movement becomes continuous, like the village, instead of snapping the player to micro-tiles. Tools still work on the underlying tile grid.
New gardens begin as hard dirt.

sections.heading: Added
items: Grass and stone textures, plus grass tufts, extend onto the surrounding scenery and menu landscape.

sections.heading: Improved
items: Removed the cottage from the garden and expanded the textured surrounding scenery.
The 3D menu has a fuller natural environment; imported models respond to lighting and weather through shared material effects.
Added a way to put the current tool away.

sections.heading: Improved
items: Natural rolling terrain replaces the uniformly flat garden surface. Ground materials are less shiny.
Improved the cloud and star sky, distant wisps and water rendering.
Grass follows the ground’s surface height.

sections.heading: Added
items: The supplied logo becomes the game and launcher icon.
A refreshed launcher shows the installed game version and download progress.
A public game page provides the Windows launcher download.
Batched 3D grass adds depth to grassy ground.

sections.heading: Garden and tools
items: Started with exportable 2 m ground chunks, each divided into nine micro-tiles, and expanded the garden to 24 × 24 metres.
Connected dirt, hard dirt, grass, long grass, water, deep water, path and stone materials; height-map parallax adds surface detail.
A low-floating spirit replaces the visible player, with mouse camera aiming, object selection and a resizing swirling cursor.
Added Hoe, Seed Packet and Watering Can models with animated use, seed and water particles, gardening interactions and saved progress.

sections.heading: People and wildlife
items: Imported Arthur and Meera with animation cycles, plus Angus and a valley visitor. Turning is smooth and NPCs avoid one another.
Added chicken, hedgehog, badger and dragon models, including procedural movement for rigged animals.
Weather-responsive shivering and talking animation/audio behaviour were explored with the visitor models.

sections.heading: Sky and sound
items: Twenty-minute days and twenty-minute nights, a moving sun, clock, stars and a changing sky.
Fair, cloudy, light rain, rain, heavy rain, thunderstorm and clearing weather, with wet ground and rain puddles.
Birds, wind, stream and storm ambience replaced the music. Layered Welsh mountains, woodland, mist, heather, ferns and gorse frame the garden.
Prototype music, the perimeter wall and fixed pond were retired as the open garden took shape.

sections.heading: Menus, guide and village
items: A 16:9 presentation and animated 3D mountain main menu, with birds, day/night weather, the golden CWTCH title and “your slice of the valley.” tagline.
Main-menu entry, new garden, options and quit controls; pause-menu Save & Quit.
An old leather Field Guide opens from its cover with animated pages, handwritten styling, 3D previews and descriptions for people, animals and plants.
Controller movement, camera, menu navigation, shoulder-button categories and directional entry selection.
A gravel village street leads to animal, plant, decoration and building shops, with cottage exteriors, interiors, purchases and delivery to the garden.

sections.heading: Development and installation
items: The desktop CWTCH folder became the canonical development project, with source assets, full source documentation and reproducible builds.
Windows launcher installation and updates use versioned packages and download checksums; saves are kept separately.
